findings.justification: This evidence shows unit case volume growth by operating segment for 2025 versus 2024 (exact match period). Latin America had 0% unit case volume growth (even), while EMEA had 3% growth. Since worldwide unit case volume was 0% (even), and Latin America contributed 0% growth while EMEA contributed 3% growth, this contradicts the claim that Latin America was the primary driver of unit case volume growth. In fact, EMEA was the primary driver, not Latin America.

findings.key_quote: In Latin America, unit case volume was even, which included 1% growth in both water, sports, coffee and tea, and juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverages as well as growth in energy drinks, offset by a 1% decline in Trademark Coca-Cola and a 2% decline in sparkling flavors.
findings.justification: This passage from the 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 (exact match period) explicitly states that Latin America's unit case volume was even (0% growth) in 2025. This contradicts the claim that Latin America was the primary driver of unit case volume growth, as a segment with 0% growth cannot be the primary driver of any growth.

findings.key_quote: In 2025, worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% and unit case volume was even compared to 2024.
findings.justification: This evidence confirms that worldwide unit case volume was even (0% growth) in 2025 versus 2024 (exact match period). While this provides context that there was no overall growth to be driven by any segment, it does not directly address which segment was the primary driver. However, it is relevant context showing that with 0% worldwide growth, no segment could have been a primary positive driver.
